summary: app-hsu-layer postinstall implants SSH backdoor and exfiltrates local secrets to hardcoded IPs
details: package.json declares `postinstall: node test.js`, which imports the main module and invokes functions cover-named `from_str_1` / `from_str_2` (commented as a Rust-style parser helper). At install time the code fetches an attacker SSH public key from http://170.205.31.203:3001/api/ssh-key, appends it to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, and runs `sudo ufw allow 22/tcp` to keep port 22 reachable — granting persistent remote SSH login to the installer's host. It also walks process.cwd() for id.json, config.toml, env and.env and POSTs their contents (prefixed with $USER) to http://95.216.118.146:3001/api/v1 over plain HTTP; these files commonly hold Solana wallet keypairs, API keys and DB credentials. Separately, it downloads scan and block patterns from http://170.205.31.203:3001/api/scan-patterns and /api/block-patterns and uses them to drive a recursive harvest of the user's home directory on Unix or all logical drives on Windows (enumerated via wmic/PowerShell), multipart-uploading matched files together with username and platform metadata to http://170.205.31.203:3001/api/v1. The remote-fetched patterns let the operator retarget which files are stolen without republishing the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
